sentence_stem: The bridge collapsed last winter, so the engineers
correct_completion: should have checked the steel more carefully.
full_sentence: The bridge collapsed last winter, so the engineers should have checked the steel more carefully.
acceptable_variants: should have inspected the welds before winter.
ought to have tested the materials earlier.

options.why_wrong: This uses a future form, but the stem describes a past failure. Criticism of a past action needs a modal perfect.

options.why_wrong: This uses the present tense, which does not match the past collapse described in the stem.

options.text: might have been wearing their coats.
options.why_wrong: This is a speculation with a modal perfect, but it has no logical link to the collapse and does not criticise anyone's work.

grammar_focus: Modal perfects for criticism of past actions (should have + past participle)
explanation: 'Should have' plus a past participle criticises a past action that did not happen. Polish speakers may choose a simple past or a conditional form here because Polish has no direct one-to-one equivalent of the English modal perfect, so the learner must remember the full pattern.
